Before we move files, Legal at ACME needs a short note on permitted uses and retention limits. Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Eval materials transfer + usage constraints

Samantha — great to hear. We can absolutely scope this as a limited-evaluation exchange. Summary of Redwood's standard commitments for MAP-level exchanges: 

- Usage: Data received for the evaluation will be used only for evaluation, model selection, and internal performance tuning tied to the ACME MAP. No redistribution or inclusion in public model releases.
- Retention: Default retention 30 days after evaluation close; can extend to 90 days with a written request and mutual approval (we log requests).
- Access controls: Files stored in a customer-scoped S3 bucket; access limited to named engineers on the MAP. Audit logs with download events available on request.
- Output handling: Generated model outputs will be treated as derivative evaluation artifacts — Redwood will not use ACME data to further train public models.

I'll attach a short draft (redwood-mpa-draft-20260115.pdf) that captures the above and includes a minimal MSA addendum for evaluation assets. We typically ask for: a scoped SFTP/Drive link, a point of contact for quartering sensitive fields, and a signed MAP addendum.

Proposed timeline (editable):
- Jan 15: ACME uploads anonymized sample (<= 2GB) to shared Drive
- Jan 16-20: Redwood runs testcases and returns results + ranked prompt pack suggestions
- Jan 21: Joint review meeting and decision on pilot expansion

I'll loop Rafael on logistics and Marissa on billing/credits. If Legal wants any adjustments to retention/usage, we can surface to our security team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Samantha — quick logistics note from ops: when you upload the testcases please include a README with the following fields: data schema, sample sizes per class, redaction steps applied, and a short set of acceptance criteria for the eval (primary sp metric + tolerance). That lets us map the MAP testcases to rack-level configs and choose an appropriate quantization/profile. Also attaching a zipped bundle if helpful — we prepared an example testcase pack (ACME_testcases_v1.zip) and a cleaned prompt pack (ACME_promptpack_v2.pdf) for you to preview.

Two operational constraints we need ACME signoff on before we run:
1) Confirm the trial may use caching to speed throughput (we log cache hits but will not persist underlying data beyond retention).
2) Confirm Redwood engineers named in the addendum are allowed to inspect anonymization steps if ACME legal requests that check.

If that's all OK, we'll schedule the runs for Jan 16-19 and share results as CSV + example model outputs.
